svg.text: Control plane — from device open to a reported page fault
One DCR pair is the only translation root. Writing its high half commits the address space: it fans satp to the walkers, flushes every TLB level, and arms a clean fault report.
host runtime
CP ring / device memory
VX_mmu_dcr (top)
VX_mmu_snoop (socket)
L2 TLB + PTW (cluster)
kernel on the cores
1 · vx_device_open — discovery and page-table construction
read CP_DEV_CAPS: bit 24 VM_ENABLED, bit 27 MMU_FAULT_REPORT
VMManager::init(): reserve the PT region in the PA allocator, allocate the root table (shadow, zeroed),
identity-map [0, USER_BASE) (IO) and [PAGE_TABLE_BASE, end) (page tables + per-warp stacks) with superpages
where alignment allows; the kernel image is identity-mapped later by mem_reserve once the loader knows it
flush(): CMD_MEM_WRITE(physical) per dirty PT page
page tables now live at VX_MEM_PAGE_TABLE_BASE_ADDR
CP_SATP_LO/HI ← satp (emulation CP DMA root; reads zero on the RTL CP)
every later vx_mem_alloc: PA from the pool, VA minted (identity or randomized), PTEs into the shadow, one flush per dirty PT page
2 · first launch — commit the address space (ensure_mmu_satp, queue-ordered ahead of CMD_LAUNCH)
CMD_DCR_WRITE SATP_LO
DCR write
satp_r[31:0] ← data (no other effect)
CMD_DCR_WRITE SATP_HI (also on Sv32, where it carries zero)
satp_r[63:32] ← data (XLEN=64)
flush_pending ← 1; fault_valid ← 0
same DCR write, forwarded down the chain
vm_active ← MODE bit (SATP_LO[31] on Sv32, SATP_HI[31:28] ≠ 0 on Sv39)
tlb_flush ← 1: dMMU + iMMU flush_if.req, held until both report done
(each clears its CAM and miss station once tlb_empty)
self-timed: no handshake back to the top — satp only changes between kernels
satp → every cluster's VX_ptw (root PPN); flush_req → L2 TLB and PTW legs
L2 TLB: waits pipe empty ∧ station idle, then clears
PTW: waits no walker active; walk cache clears on req
done = both legs; the top ANDs every cluster
cluster_flush_done → flush_pending ← 0
CMD_LAUNCH (then CMD_CACHE_FLUSH, COUT drain, …)
KMU dispatch; __vx_cta_entry does `csrw satp` — a readback mirror, not a translation source
from here every dcache/icache request is translated at the socket MMU under vm_active; hits cost one registered stage, misses walk as in the miss sequence figure
3 · a page fault — structural fault in the walker, first-fault latch, host readback
a lane touches an unmapped page → L1 miss → L2 miss → walk
walker: ¬V (or ¬leaf at level 0, or misaligned) → RESP fault=1
fault_if pulses {va, access, amo}; the fill carries fault=1 to L2, L1
L1 station drains the entry as kills: loads/AMOs get a zeroed reply,
stores and fetches retire silently; nothing installs at any level
cluster_fault_valid / va / access / amo
first fault only: fault_valid ← 1, {va, access, amo} latched (lowest cluster index wins a tie)
later faults are ignored until the host clears the report
check_mmu_fault() after the launch: CMD_DCR_READ FAULT_INFO
{amo[3], access[2:1], valid[0]} — latched at the read, held until the next DCR access (pulse-then-poll)
read FAULT_VA, FAULT_VA_HI; write FAULT_INFO (clear) → VX_ERR_DEVICE_LOST, "device page fault on write in page 0x…"
SimX: the same latch lives in Ptw::fault_; the processor loop ends the launch as soon as a fault is latched and the fabric is quiet, since a
killed fetch owes no response. In RTL the warp drains on its kill replies; a fetch fault stalls that warp until the host tears the launch down.
